The coupon book has a new reward. Until now, ten stamps earned one free round. Now, on top of that, every one hundred rounds earns a souvenir. One hundred, two hundred, three hundred, and so on.

Here is how rounds are counted. Paid rounds, which are the stamps, plus free rounds used. A free round has no stamp, but it is still a round played. For example, ninety-one stamps plus nine free rounds used is exactly one hundred rounds.

Staff see this on the tee sheet bill. Put that player's green fee on the bill and a pink Souvenir due row appears. If they are not there yet, a small grey line shows progress, like thirty-seven out of one hundred.

Hand over the souvenir and press Gave souvenir. It is a physical gift, so the bill total does not change. One souvenir line goes in the ledger, and the row turns to Souvenir given. If it was pressed by mistake, Undo takes it back.

Customers see this on the coupon screen in the app. Under the stamp card there is a progress bar to one hundred rounds. When it fills, a banner says a souvenir is waiting. After pickup, it shows in their history.

A few exceptions. Members do not collect stamps, so their rounds do not add up. Guests not linked to an app account do not appear on the bill. And if a refund removes a stamp, the round count drops with it.

Here is where things stand. The code is deployed in both apps. What remains is running two SQL files in order: GPS 0029 first, then 0138. Until then the souvenir rows stay hidden and billing works as usual. The button on the staff F and B screen is not deployed yet.
